title: Cap. VIII: Type major limited — better argue from type to antitype
pass_a_gloss: Next the argument can be dissolved without trouble. As to the major: the proposition 'What is shown in the thing represented by a type must have preceded in the type' needs this limit — if the type was in fact set up to represent that thing. Otherwise often many things appear in the represented matter that one type could not show, so several types are used to sketch the same thing. Even with that limit the proposition is true only as far as the nature of the type-thing can bear, keeping the difference between type and antitype, shadow and body. So arguing from type to the shadowed thing is better than from the thing back to the type.
pass_b_english: Next, this argument can be dissolved without any trouble. For as to the major: the proposition "What is exhibited in the thing represented by a type must have preceded in the type" needs this limitation — if, that is, the type was set up to represent that thing. For otherwise often many things have been exhibited in the represented matter which could not be represented by one type; and for that reason several have been employed to sketch the same thing. Then even when that limitation is applied, the proposition is not true except so far as the nature of the thing which is the type can bear, the difference between Type and antitype (τὸ ἀντίτυπον), shadow and body, being kept. Therefore argumentation from the type to the thing shadowed is better than from this latter back to the former.
source_text: Deinde nullo negotio dissolvi potest hoc argumentum. Ad majorem enim quod attinet, propositio, Quod in re per typum representata exhibetur, illud in typo praecessisse oportuit. Eget hac limitatione, si nempe ad id representandum typus fuit comparatus. Nam alioqui saepenumero multa in re representata exhibita fuerunt, quae non potuerunt uno typo representari; quapropter multi ad eandem rem adumbrandam adhibiti sunt. Deinde etiam adhibita illa limitatione propositio vera non est, nisi quantum pati potest ejus rei, quae typus est, natura, servata inter Typum & τὸ ἀντίτυπον, umbram & corpus differentia. Itaque melior est a typo ad rem adumbratam, quam ab hac ad illam argumentatio.

choices.decision: Same antitype lock as 65; umbram & corpus kept
